bands.2045: 20-45 Hz, mean PSD over kept bins x 25 Hz -> uV^2
bands.65: 65-120 Hz, mean PSD over kept bins x 55 Hz -> uV^2

method.slope: least-squares slope of log10 PSD on log10 f over kept 15-45 Hz bins
method.bursts: 2 s windows whose 20-45 Hz power exceeds 3x the session median over task windows, per channel; either channel counts; no exclusion
method.good_window: no channel > 150 uV peak after 1-40 Hz band-pass, no blink sample (blinkmask 100 uV), AF 60 Hz pick-up < 200 uV^2/Hz
method.per_minute: mean over good windows, bootstrap 95 % CI (2000 resamples)
method.drift: Theil-Sen over per-minute values, 95 % interval, per 10 min
method.matched_minutes: paired log10 difference per shared minute, bootstrap CI over minutes, sign-flip permutation p
method.lit_vs_dark: each lit window paired with the nearest dark window of the same stage within 45 s; sign-flip p
method.same_bins: the same kept bins are used in every window of every session, so stage, run and day comparisons are on identical bins

notes: Muse AF7/AF8 LSB is 0.40 uV; during the task their 20-45 Hz power is a few uV^2 (1.5-3 uV rms), near the device floor: sustained frontalis contraction would be 10-100x this and is not seen, but tension below ~1 uV rms is unmeasurable here.
The 65-120 Hz band sits on the Muse anti-alias roll-off (PSD falls ~100x from 65 to 120 Hz); it is reported relative to itself only.

vr_planes9: before the first flicker the forehead electrodes were off the skin (AF 60 Hz pick-up > 6000 uV^2/Hz) until about 2 minutes before; the last minute is the headset being settled, not a relaxed baseline. The ear electrodes carried a 60 Hz line of ~2-3e4 uV^2/Hz through run 1 (poor ear contact), hence the wide mains cut.
vr_planes10: TP10 was loose (22 % of task windows above 150 uV, broadband noise 10x TP9), so ratios to TP10 and to the TP pair are not comparable between runs; the TP9 ratio is the one to read.
Per-minute Theil-Sen intervals treat minutes as independent; window-level slopes are also given but their intervals are too narrow (autocorrelation).
